name: Sleep Current Profiler
blurb: average current from sleep and wake times and currents
intro: A device wakes once per period, runs through a few active states, then sleeps for the rest. The average current is the charge of every state per period divided by the period; states that run only every Nth wake are spread over their own interval. The breakdown shows which state to optimise first.

inputs.label: Wake-up period
inputs.help: Time from one wake-up to the next.

inputs.label: Sleep current
inputs.help: Whole board while asleep: MCU, regulator quiescent, pull-ups, sensors.

inputs.label: Active states per wake-up
inputs.help: Current in A (5m = 5 mA), time in s (2m = 2 ms). 'Every' = runs once every N wake-ups (1 = each time).

examples.title: Sensor node: read every 10 s, send every minute

usage: Give the wake-up period in seconds, the sleep current in A, and the active states as a table of {name, i (A), t (s), every (run once per N wake-ups)}, plus the supply in volts. It returns the average current, the duty cycle, charge per period and per day (mAh/day), average power and energy per day, and each state's share of the average. Feed the average current into the battery life estimator.
sources: I_avg = [Σ I_k · t_k / N_k + I_sleep · (T − Σ t_k / N_k)] / T: charge balance over one period (definition), the same method as TI application report SWRA349 'Coin cells and peak current draw'
